outcome: delivery route (caesarean section, vaginal birth, instrumental delivery)
complications in the fourth stage of labor
cohort: The study included 205 women, comprising 104 with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at the time of labor and 101 randomly selected women without infection.
finding: Maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection generally did not negatively affect obstetric outcomes, but was associated with a longer duration of hospitalization and more frequent labor complications.
mod_finding: No statistically significant difference was found in the frequency of caesarean section, vaginal birth, instrumental delivery, or type of childbirth initiation between SARS-CoV-2 infected and control groups.
